question.text: At the time of seeking registration or launching a new regular Cat II AIF scheme, the PPM is filed with SEBI through whom?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 78), AIFs file their Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) with SEBI through a SEBI-registered merchant banker at the time of seeking registration or launching a new regular scheme. The merchant banker acts as a gatekeeper and provides observations on the PPM before submission. The Trap: Auditor-direct and IA-direct routes are not permitted. RBI/FEMA is for forex filings, not SEBI AIF registration. Note that SEBI provides observations on the PPM; it does not 'approve' the PPM itself. Note: Per page 188, SEBI does not approve the PPM, and Large Value Fund (LVF) schemes are exempt from the merchant-banker PPM filing requirement that applies to regular AIF schemes.
